summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with a complex history including systemic lupus erythematosus, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, recent septic arthritis, and coronary artery disease presented with substernal chest pain concerning for acute cardiac ischemia. She was found to have elevated troponin and severe hyperkalemia, which resolved with dialysis and calcium. Due to a history of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, she was treated with bivalirudin and nitroglycerin for presumed unstable angina, though no acute coronary occlusion was confirmed. Her chest pain resolved, and cardiac medications were optimized, including increasing atorvastatin to 80 mg daily. She also underwent a left popliteal artery angioplasty for peripheral artery disease with gangrene of the left toes; amputation was planned as an outpatient. Her chronic gastrointestinal bleeding from gastric polyps persisted, precluding Plavix restart. She was discharged to an extended care facility with stable cardiac status, improved potassium, and ongoing management of anemia, vascular disease, and lupus.
problems: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of extremities with gangrene, left leg
Iron deficiency anemia secondary to blood loss (chronic)
Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
